metadata.summary: Manchester United have completed the signing of midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton.
metadata.content: Carlos Baleba transfer: Manchester United complete signing of Cameroon midfielder from Brighton | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Breaking Carlos Baleba transfer: Manchester United complete signing of Cameroon midfielder from Brighton Sky Sports News has been reporting on United's interest in Baleba since last autumn and broke the news that they enquired about signing him during the January transfer window; the Cameroon international signs a five-year deal at Old Trafford Tuesday 25 August 2026 17:23, UK Image: Carlos Baleba has joined Manchester United from Brighton Manchester United have completed the signing of midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton. The Cameroon international, 22, joins the club in a deal worth up to £70m, made up of a £65m guaranteed fee plus £5m in add-ons. He has signed a five-year contract which includes the option of a further year. Baleba is currently injured, having picked up an ankle injury in pre-season, but Sky Sports News understands he could be back by mid-September. messages.text: Warren thinks Fury-AJ fight will go ahead in America

metadata.summary: Frank Warren says he thinks a long-awaited heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will go ahead in America despite claims the bout is in doubt.
metadata.content: Tyson Fury fight with Anthony Joshua will go ahead in 2026 in America, predicts promoter Frank Warren | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Exclusive Tyson Fury fight with Anthony Joshua will go ahead in 2026 in America, predicts promoter Frank Warren Talks are ongoing over a possible November blockbuster clash between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua; an apparent dispute over the location of the fight led to Fury claiming that the event was in "serious doubt" Tuesday 25 August 2026 15:14, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Boxing promoter Frank Warren says he expects to see the much-anticipated heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua in early November but says there are still plenty of negotiations that need to happen first. Frank Warren says he thinks a long-awaited heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will go ahead in America despite claims the bout is in doubt. Everything seemed to be in place for the British pair of former world champions to meet in London in November, but Saudi organisers Sela's desire to instead hold the event in the USA has created a hold up. Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has been pushing to keep the fight in London, which led to Fury claiming last week that the contest was in "serious doubt" because his rival was asking for "more money". metadata.summary: A furious Joe Root vowed England would earn back the trust of the nation after his return as Test captain was overshadowed by the latest off-field incident to rock English cricket.
metadata.content: Joe Root: Furious England captain 'hacked off' after Brydon Carse incident overshadows Pakistan victory | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content Joe Root: Furious England captain 'hacked off' after Brydon Carse incident overshadows Pakistan victory Joe Root "hacked off" by "stupid mistakes" as off-field controversy involving Brydon Carse overshadows his successful return as Test captain; watch the second England vs Pakistan Test live on Sky Sports from Thursday Jack Wilkinson Sports Journalist @jacktwilkinson Tuesday 25 August 2026 15:16, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joe Root gives his view on the latest incident involving an England player at a nightclub, after video footage emerged of Brydon Carse in handcuffs on Saturday night. A furious Joe Root vowed England would earn back the trust of the nation after his return as Test captain was overshadowed by the latest off-field incident to rock English cricket. England swept Pakistan away by an innings and 103 runs inside three days at Headingley to hand Root victory on his comeback as Test captain. Within 24 hours, video footage emerged of England fast bowler Brydon Carse being handcuffed and led away by police on Saturday night after Durham's players had gone out to celebrate their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship. messages.text: 'Not the best version of me' - Hamilton regrets frustrated Dutch GP comments

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton says he didn't present "the best version" of himself when criticising his Ferrari team over the radio and in television interviews at the Dutch Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver 'takes responsibility' for frustrated radio and media comments at Dutch GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver 'takes responsibility' for frustrated radio and media comments at Dutch GP Lewis Hamilton was critical of his Ferrari team during and after Sunday's Dutch Grand Prix; Hamilton was frustrated at Ferrari allowing him to be held up by his team-mate Charles Leclerc; watch the Italian Grand Prix at Monza live on Sky Sports F1 on September 4-6 Tuesday 25 August 2026 11:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton was left frustrated with Ferrari for 'wasting time' by not swapping him and Charles Leclerc earlier. Lewis Hamilton says he didn't present "the best version" of himself when criticising his Ferrari team over the radio and in television interviews at the Dutch Grand Prix. Hamilton sounded irate in a series of radio messages sent when he was being held up by team-mate Charles Leclerc despite the pair being on different strategies during the race in Zandvoort. The seven-time world champion felt as though the lost time ultimately cost him a podium as he finished fourth just behind George Russell having been unable to overtake the Mercedes in an exciting finale. messages.text: Leeds and Rangers co-owner York arrested

metadata.summary: Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.
metadata.content: Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York arrested in Ohio and pleads no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York arrested in Ohio and pleads no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools Jed York, who owns San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct; York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio; He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences By Adrian Kajumba and Sahil Jaidka Tuesday 25 August 2026 16:20, UK Image: Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools. Court records show that York, who owns the San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct. York was charged with possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to an undercover online prostitution advertisement, according to prosecutors. York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio, near where he was born and raised in Youngstown. He was released after posting a $5,000 bond. He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offence
